catalog_quote: Ci sono due tipi diversi di tono (intonazione della parola) in slavisano. Si trova da una parte il tono normale o „discendente“ che corrisponde a quello dell’italiano ... p. es. dvignit [»dvignit] ‘sollevare’. Dall’altra c’è anche un tono che noi chiamiamo – secondo la tradizione slavistica – „ascendente“, ma che si distingue considerevolmente dal tono indicato con questo termine nella linguistica croata e serba. Si tratta più che altro di una doppia accentazione di due sillabe successive di uguale forza o con più forza sulla seconda sillaba, anche se spesso accompagnata in effetti da un aumento della frequenza fondamentale (f0). ... Il tono ascendente slavisano risale come quello croato all’antica ritrazione di accento štocava ma è produttivo anche nei prestiti ... sweep_summary: Slavomolisano (slav1254) is in the catalog as 'tonal' on Breu & Piccoli 2000 (grammar part of the Acquaviva dictionary). The title sweep produced exactly one item, Vitale, Boula de Mareüil & De Meo 2017 on Chinese L2 Italian polar questions, which Glottolog's own reference page says was attached to svm by a computerized assignment on the word 'sviluppo' — not relevant, priority none. Crossref returned nothing new on Molise Slavic accent) and Breu's Konstanz 'acqua' site. From that site I fetched sources the catalog's deciding source itself, 38 pp...), with; the catalog quotation is verbatim at p. 388, and p. 389 adds that the two tones are distinctive only on the first/only syllable (minimal pairs nos/nos, bila/bila, kupit/kupit) and that length is contrastive only under the falling tone. Rešetar 1911 §§72-74 (on file from the 9/16 pass) independently confirms a new-Štokavian accent position with frequent double accentuation. Coding 'tonal' stands; no source read contradicts it. Still unread and print-only (from the existing wishlist, not from this sweep's items): Barone 1995 phonology of Acquaviva (high), Breu 1999 'Phonologie und Verbkonjugation im Moliseslavischen' (medium), Sammartino 2004 grammar of Montemitro (medium).

new_statements.translation: It is above all a double accentuation of two successive syllables of equal force or with more force on the second syllable, though often in fact accompanied by a rise in fundamental frequency (f0). [...] The tones are distinctive only on the first or – unlike in Croatian – on the only syllable of the word. As minimal pairs we cite e.g. nos 'nose' : nos 'carry! (imper. sg. of nosit)' or bila 'been (ppp of bit)' : bila 'white' for long vowels, and kupit 'to gather' : kupit 'to buy' for short ones.

new_statements.reading: First-hand description of the Acquaviva Collecroce variety by the leading specialist. Two word-tones ('discendente' = ordinary single stress as in Italian; 'ascendente' = a double accentuation over two successive syllables, or over the two moras of one long syllable, usually with an f0 rise). The tones are lexically contrastive and are contrastive only on the first (or only) syllable of the word (minimal pairs given); vowel length is contrastive only under the falling tone. Position of the falling accent is not given by a rule in this section; the rising accent is inherited from the Štokavian retraction and is productive in loans. This is the same passage the catalog quotes (catalog_quote found verbatim at p. 388), so it confirms the current 'tonal' coding rather than superseding it. Rešetar 1911 (Ital. transl., e-ed. 2001, §§72-74, pp. 107-109, already on file as RES-3) adds the position statement that the dialect follows the new-Štokavian principle as to accent POSITION ('va decisamente definita come basantesi – per quanto riguarda la posizione dell'accento – sul principio dell'accentazione štocava nuova', §73 p. 108) with frequent double accentuation (stronger on the original syllable, higher/rising on the preceding one) — the historical antecedent of Breu's 'tono ascendente'.
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences

new_statements.second_reader_bearing_note: Bearing stands: the passage confirms the catalog's 'tonal' coding (two lexically contrastive word tones on the first/only syllable, with minimal pairs; quantity contrastive only under the falling tone; accent position additionally lexical/mobile per secs 2.1.2 and 3.1-3.2). Only the Rešetar locator needs correcting: §73 with the 'basantesi... posizione dell'accento' sentence is on p. 109 of the 2001 e-edition (PDF page 23), and cap. 3 §§72-74 spans pp. 108-110, not §73 p. 108 / pp. 107-109.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all parts of the deciding quotation, the domain quote and the exceptions quote were found verbatim in the held Breu & Piccoli 2000 grammar text at the stated sections/pages (1.2 pp. 388-389; 2.1.2 p. 394), and the two corroborating held Breu texts (HSK 2014 p. 2113; ESLO 2020 preprint) say the same. (2) Deciding source: a first-hand grammar sketch inside a dictionary (2000/2011) by the leading specialist, restated by him in 2014 and 2020; Rešetar 1911 (fetched sources now from Breu's Konstanz site, §§72-73) independently describes the same Neo-Štokavian-derived system with incomplete retraction realised as double accentuation and rising accent possible on monosyllables — it confirms the TONAL-OR-PITCH-ACCENT / lexical-position coding. (3) Better sources exist but are print-only: Barone 1995 (447-pp. phonology of the same village) is the obvious gap and Breu flags disagreements '
